summary: Tests that user data sent out of the server never includes passwords or email addresses, and that no route or component selects whole user rows.
purpose: Protects private user fields from leaking to browsers.
why: Likely reason: the public user shape should be the only user data that leaves the server.
how: Defines a search pattern for passwords, hashes, test emails and email fields. Checks the public user conversion keeps only avatar, id, name and xp, even from a full row with secrets. Checks crew detail, crew lists, contest entries and standings contain no private fields and report the right names and points. Scans the app, component and domain source files for whole-user selections.
inputs: Test users and fantasy team data, plus the source files in the project.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test.
risks: The source scan uses a text pattern and can miss a leak written another way. The leak pattern matches the word password anywhere, so a legitimate field containing it would fail.
debug: If a payload test fails, search the output for the matched text. If the source scan fails, the failure lists the files that match.
